The evidence found does not establish a separately bounded market town with its own population in 1622. The proposed market_town type is retained from the supplied need-list only as a provisional classification; confirm whether the settlement should instead be represented as a fort-associated locality or whether site_panhala should be omitted as duplicative.

The 2011 Census source identifies Velhe as a sub-district, not enough by itself to prove a distinct 1622 village. Confirm exact historic name and village/town classification.

Modern visitor material calls Tikona Peth the nearest village to Tikona Fort. No pre-1622 attestation of the settlement or the compound name Tikona Peth was established. Keep valid_from null until a dated record is found.
The 2011 Census confirms a present-day village named Gunjavane in Pune district, but not its existence or name in 1622. The site is a provisional locality anchor for Murumbdev Fort only.

The Pune District government identifies Kondhana Fort at present-day Donaje, and the 2011 Census lists Donaje. These references do not date Donaje as a settlement in 1622. Keep Kondhana as the period fort name; do not backdate Sinhagad.

Chaudenson (1997) states that Korlai village was founded around 1595; it is an approximate date summarized from earlier work, not a dated foundation inscription presented in the article. HPIP records Korlai/Kôrlê as forms. Confirm the exact spelling used locally in 1622.

Modern government tourism material locates Janjira Fort near Murud, but no source in this pass dates a separate Murud town to 1622. The existing site_rajapuri remains the immediate shore/landing anchor; site_murud is a secondary mainland support locator only. Verify historical status and whether both sites are needed.
